key_insight: Training variational quantum algorithms is strongly NP-hard even when the goal is only to find a local minimum, not the global optimum.
engineering_relevance: This means there is no general polynomial-time guarantee for reliably training VQAs, so practical performance will depend heavily on circuit structure, problem instance, and heuristic optimization choices.
method: Prove strong NP-hardness for locating a local minimum of a Hermitian trigonometric polynomial.
Construct quantum circuits whose VQA training objectives encode these hard instances.
Reduce the local-minimization problem to VQA training in polynomial time, including hardness within \u2113p distance < \u03c0/2 of a local minimizer.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical complexity result: the authors show a polynomial-time reduction and strong NP-hardness, with no experimental dataset or empirical benchmark.
watch_item: This is a worst-case hardness result, so it does not rule out good performance on structured real-world instances or with specialized ansatz/optimizers.
paper_title: Training Variational Quantum Algorithms Is NP-Hard, Even Locally
